standard.name: Acyclic linear Gaussian structural equation model
One stochastic perfect single-node intervention per node
Effective-intervention condition specialized to centered perfect interventions

assumptions.condition: The weights satisfy \(\pi_c>0\) for every \(c\in C\) and \(\sum_{c\in C}\pi_c=1\).
The observations \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) are independent draws from \(P_{\mathrm{mix}}\).

definitions.name: Fully covered unlabeled perfect-surgery class \(\mathcal M_p\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_p=\{(G,B,\omega,\tau,\{\Sigma_c,\pi_c\}_{c\in C}):\Sigma_0=A^{-1}\Omega A^{-\top},\ \Sigma_j=(A^{(j)})^{-1}\Omega^{(j)}(A^{(j)})^{-\top}\ \forall j\in V,\ [\operatorname{Pa}(j)\neq\varnothing\ \text{or}\ \tau_j\neq\omega_j]\ \forall j\in V,\ \pi_c>0\ \forall c\in C,\ \sum_{c\in C}\pi_c=1\}\).

definitions.name: Coordinate-isolated precision pair
definitions.construction: A pair \(\{c,d\}\subset C\) is coordinate-isolated at \(r\in V\) exactly when \(K_c-K_d=s e_re_r^{\top}\) for some \(s\neq0\).

definitions.name: Semantic explanation
definitions.construction: \(\theta_{\mathrm{sem}}=(c_0,\vartheta,G,B,\omega,\tau,\pi)\), where \(c_0\) is an input position and \(\vartheta:C\setminus\{c_0\}\to V\) is a bijection.

definitions.name: Coordinate certificate \(\mathsf{Cert}\)
definitions.construction: Given an unordered \(p+1\)-tuple \(\{(\Sigma_c,\pi_c)\}\), check positive definiteness, distinctness, and weights; invert every covariance; find and orient a coordinate-isolated pair using a third component's marginal; form every support \(\operatorname{rowsupp}(K_c-K_{c_0})\); repeatedly match a component whose residual support contains one unmatched coordinate; recover each row by baseline regression; then verify \(K_{c_0}=A^{\top}\Omega^{-1}A\) and, for every matched pair \(\vartheta(c)=j\), verify \(K_c-K_{c_0}=\tau_j^{-1}e_je_j^{\top}-\omega_j^{-1}a_ja_j^{\top}\).

definitions.name: Thresholded coordinate decoder \(\widehat{\mathsf R}_{\alpha,g}\)
definitions.construction: Invert \(\widehat\Sigma_c\); detect an entry of \(\widehat K_c-\widehat K_d\) when its magnitude exceeds \(\alpha/2\); recognize a coordinate pair by one detected diagonal and no other detected entry; orient it toward the endpoint whose corresponding marginal is closer to any third component; then apply singleton row-support matching.

definitions.name: Rank-only baseline information
definitions.construction: \(R_{cd}=\operatorname{rank}(K_c-K_d)\) and \(r_c=\sum_{d\neq c}R_{cd}\); a rank-only selector is a component-permutation-equivariant map from \(R\) to one vertex of \(C\).

definitions.name: Two-node chain counterfamilies
definitions.construction: For \(1\to2\), set \(B_{21}=b\neq0\), \(\omega=(u,v)\), and \(\tau=(t,s)\), so \(\Sigma_0=\begin{pmatrix}u&bu\\bu&b^2u+v\end{pmatrix}\), \(\Sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}t&bt\\bt&b^2t+v\end{pmatrix}\), and \(\Sigma_2=\operatorname{diag}(u,s)\); use \((b,u,v,t,s)=(2,1,1,3,2)\) and \((1,1,1,1/2,2)\) as legal witnesses.

definitions.name: One-root star rank-obstruction family
definitions.construction: For every \(p\ge2\), take the one-root star with root \(1\), edges \(1\to j\) of coefficients \(b_j\neq0\) for \(j=2,\ldots,p\), positive baseline variances \(\omega_j\), and positive intervention variances \(\tau_j\). Put \(d=\tau_1^{-1}-\omega_1^{-1}\neq0\) and restrict to the nonempty strict region \(d(\tau_j-\omega_j)-b_j^2<0\) for every leaf \(j\).

definitions.name: Three-node fork counterfamily
definitions.construction: Take the fork \(1\to2\), \(1\to3\) with coefficients \(2\) and \(3\), \(\omega=(1,1,1)\), and \(\tau=(3,4,5)\); its pairwise rank matrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}0&1&2&2\\1&0&2&2\\2&2&0&3\\2&2&3&0\end{pmatrix}\). Retain the open parameter neighborhood on which these ranks remain unchanged.

definitions.name: Local-surgery false-positive tuple
definitions.construction: In dimension three, let \(K_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&2&-1\\0&-1&2\end{pmatrix}\) and \(K_j=K_0+e_je_j^{\top}\) for \(j=1,2,3\).

definitions.name: Near-singular all-component conditioning family
definitions.construction: For \(0<t<1/3\), let \(\Sigma_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}\), \(\Sigma_1(t)=\begin{pmatrix}t&t\\t&1+t\end{pmatrix}\), \(\Sigma_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\), and perturb only component one to \(\widehat\Sigma_1(t)=\begin{pmatrix}t&2t\\2t&1+t\end{pmatrix}\).

definitions.name: Growing-component estimation handle
definitions.construction: Apply a separation-preserving sum-of-squares projection and recursive partial clustering to the centered pooled sample, estimate each recovered cluster covariance with effective-rank control, and permutation-match the resulting \(p+1\) covariance estimates before passing them to the coordinate certificate.

statements.statement: Every member of \(\mathcal M_p\) has \(p+1\) distinct covariance matrices, and the pooled law \(P_{\mathrm{mix}}\) identifies the unordered covariance-weight pairs \(\{(\Sigma_c,\pi_c):c\in C\}\) up to permutation.
statements.justification: This lemma closes the population passage from a pooled distribution to the unordered component tuple.
statements.gap: Kumar, Shiragur, and Uhler identify general mixture parameters for fixed component count; this lemma isolates the exact population fact required when the causal labels are still hidden.
statements.consumer: Theorem 1 can start from the pooled law rather than assuming that component covariances arrive with semantic labels.

statements.statement: For every \(j\in V\), writing \(a_j=A^{\top}e_j\), the perfect surgery obeys \(\Delta_j=\tau_j^{-1}e_je_j^{\top}-\omega_j^{-1}a_ja_j^{\top}\) and \(\operatorname{rowsupp}(\Delta_j)=\{j\}\cup\operatorname{Pa}(j)\), including when a nonroot has \(\tau_j=\omega_j\).
statements.justification: The exact row support is the information discarded by the published rank compression.
statements.gap: Squires et al. give a rank-two difference identity, while Varici et al. exploit sparse precision differences for labeled pairs; neither states this universal unlabeled perfect-surgery row-support equality with unchanged nonroot variance allowed.
statements.consumer: The row supports drive baseline recognition, unique target matching, and the stability threshold.

statements.statement: A pair \(\{c,d\}\subset C\) is coordinate-isolated at \(r\in V\) if and only if its endpoints are the baseline and the perfect intervention on a root \(r\); for any third component, exactly the baseline endpoint has the same \(r\)-th marginal variance as that third component.
statements.justification: This is the permutation-equivariant replacement for minimizing pairwise rank sums.
statements.gap: Proposition 10 of Squires et al. attempts baseline recovery from ranks; no cited result characterizes baseline-root pairs by exact coordinate support and orients them by an invariant marginal.
statements.consumer: Theorem 1 obtains the baseline without faithfulness, a known root, or an externally supplied observational sample.

statements.statement: For every member of \(\mathcal M_p\), the pooled law \(P_{\mathrm{mix}}\) uniquely determines \(\theta_{\mathrm{sem}}\). After identifying \(c_0\), each nonbaseline component \(c\) has support \(S_c=\operatorname{rowsupp}(K_c-K_{c_0})\); the unique bijection satisfies \(\vartheta(c)\in S_c\), and then \(\operatorname{Pa}(j)=S_{\vartheta^{-1}(j)}\setminus\{j\}\), \(B_{j,\operatorname{Pa}(j)}^{\top}=(\Sigma_{c_0})_{\operatorname{Pa}(j),\operatorname{Pa}(j)}^{-1}(\Sigma_{c_0})_{\operatorname{Pa}(j),j}\), \(\omega_j=(\Sigma_{c_0})_{jj}-(\Sigma_{c_0})_{j,\operatorname{Pa}(j)}(\Sigma_{c_0})_{\operatorname{Pa}(j),\operatorname{Pa}(j)}^{-1}(\Sigma_{c_0})_{\operatorname{Pa}(j),j}\), and \(\tau_j=(\Sigma_{\vartheta^{-1}(j)})_{jj}\).
statements.justification: The theorem identifies the baseline, targets, full DAG, coefficients, all variances, and attached mixture weights at every legal parameter point.
statements.gap: Squires et al. recover a broader latent representation under their setup but their unknown-baseline Proposition 10 is false. Kumar and Sinha (2021, Theorem 3.1) identify the intervention tuples and weights in a pooled mixture of perfect interventions only when the finite discrete baseline causal Bayesian network and its observational law are given, under positivity and exclusion. Kumar et al. provide the baseline separately for causal discovery and invoke interventional faithfulness. None identifies the hidden observational component and the full centered-Gaussian SEM explanation from the unordered mixture alone.
statements.consumer: Pooled perfect-intervention studies obtain a uniquely labeled structural Gaussian model without a designated control sample.

statements.statement: The coordinate certificate \(\mathsf{Cert}\) accepts an arbitrary unordered \(p+1\)-tuple if and only if it has an explanation in \(\mathcal M_p\); on acceptance it returns the unique \(\theta_{\mathrm{sem}}\), and on rejection it returns a violated positive-definiteness, orientation, matching, baseline-factorization, or surgery equality. Its worst-case cost is \(O(p^4)\) exact real-arithmetic operations and \(O(p^3)\) storage.
statements.justification: Identification alone cannot distinguish a legal perfect-surgery tuple from an algebraic impostor; soundness and completeness make the reconstruction semantically auditable.
statements.gap: Appendix G of Squires et al. explicitly leaves full membership testing open and tests only a necessary rank condition. Kumar and Sinha (2021, Theorem 3.1) recover intervention tuples relative to a given finite discrete baseline causal Bayesian network and observational law; they do not certify whether an arbitrary unordered Gaussian component tuple admits one common hidden-baseline SEM and all claimed perfect surgeries.
statements.consumer: A pooled-data pipeline can reject component collections that cannot arise from one common baseline DAG before invoking causal interpretation.

statements.statement: Theorem 2 strictly replaces the unknown-baseline promise of Proposition 10 in Squires et al. on the observed-coordinate fully covered perfect-intervention subclass: both two-node constructions are legal members of \(\mathcal M_2\), the first gives literal scores \((3,2,2)\) and symmetric scores \((3,3,4)\), the second gives symmetric scores \((3,2,3)\), and the legal three-node fork gives literal scores \((5,4,5,5)\); in each case the coordinate certificate returns the true baseline and explanation.
statements.justification: Low-dimensional legal families locate the failed rank inequality and prevent the replacement theorem from being presented as a mere alternative algorithm.
statements.gap: The published proposition asserts unique rank-score minimization; the displayed legal families falsify both its literal formula and the natural symmetric repair.
statements.consumer: Users of the ICML reduction obtain a valid baseline preprocessing step and explicit regression tests for implementations.

statements.statement: For every \(p\ge2\), the one-root star construction contains a nonempty strict-inequality parameter region on which the pairwise rank matrix \(R\) is invariant under swapping the baseline with the root-intervention vertex. Consequently, no component-permutation-equivariant rank-only selector universally recovers the baseline on \(\mathcal M_p\).
statements.justification: The obstruction shows that the correction needs entrywise support and marginal information, rather than a different scalar aggregation of the same ranks.
statements.gap: Squires et al. use one rank score, but the literature does not establish an open-family impossibility for the entire class of equivariant rank-only selectors.
statements.consumer: Method designers can rule out every rank-only baseline heuristic and focus on information-preserving summaries.

statements.statement: If \(E_{\mathrm{op}}<\varepsilon_{\star}\), then after permutation matching every \(\widehat\Sigma_c\) is positive definite, every precision-difference entry has error below \(\alpha/4\), and the thresholded coordinate decoder recovers \(c_0\), \(\vartheta\), and \(G\) exactly. The condition uses the minimum eigenvalue across all components, not only the baseline.
statements.justification: The resolvent radius converts population identification into a deterministic error interface for any component estimator.
statements.gap: The cited causal-discovery papers do not give an all-component operator-norm neighborhood guaranteeing unknown-baseline and exact target recovery without faithfulness.
statements.consumer: Any future mixture estimator with a permutation-matched operator tail inherits a finite-sample discrete-recovery bound by event inclusion.

statements.statement: In the near-singular family, the baseline minimum eigenvalue is fixed, \(\alpha=1/2\), and \(g>1/2\), yet \(\|\widehat\Sigma_1(t)-\Sigma_1(t)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=t\to0\) and every estimated precision pair has a detected off-diagonal entry. At \(t=1/100\), the three off-diagonal magnitudes are \(103/97\), \(1\), and \(200/97\). Thus no positive radius depending only on baseline conditioning, \(\alpha\), and \(g\) can certify this inverse-threshold decoder.
statements.justification: This boundary result explains why the stability theorem conditions every component rather than concealing near-singular interventions.
statements.gap: No cited result isolates this conditioning failure for unknown-baseline perfect-intervention decoding.
statements.consumer: Finite-sample implementations learn which eigenvalue margin must be monitored before reporting a stable causal explanation.

statements.statement: The three-dimensional false-positive tuple passes singleton support matching and every local diagonal surgery check for an apparent empty DAG, but fails \(K_{c_0}=A^{\top}\Omega^{-1}A\); it therefore has no explanation in \(\mathcal M_3\).
statements.justification: The example makes the baseline factorization check logically necessary for certificate soundness.
statements.gap: The necessary rank screen in Squires et al. does not reject all tuples whose local differences mimic atomic interventions.
statements.consumer: Certificate implementers receive a minimal false-positive test that catches omission of the global common-baseline constraint.

statements.statement: Using the growing-component estimation handle, construct a concrete estimator from \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) and derive an explicit \(T_n(\delta)\) such that \(\Pr\{E_{\mathrm{op}}>T_n(\delta)\}\le\delta\) when the number of centered Gaussian components is \(p+1\); characterize primitive weight, spectral-envelope, and pairwise-separation conditions under which \(T_n(\delta)<\varepsilon_{\star}\) with sample size polynomial in \(p\), and determine whether the perfect-surgery geometry weakens the near-disjoint total-variation separation required by generic centered-mixture clustering.
statements.justification: This is the unresolved end-to-end statistical bottleneck rather than an assumed component-estimation oracle.
statements.gap: Kumar et al. fix the component count, while Anderson et al. cluster growing centered mixtures under strong total-variation separation but do not deliver the surgery-specific operator-error tail consumed here.
statements.consumer: A solution would turn the deterministic certificate into a growing-dimensional guarantee for genuinely pooled intervention samples.

sampling_model.design: Population identification from one pooled centered Gaussian mixture; the open statistical extension uses independent pooled draws.
sampling_model.units: Independent vectors \(Z_i\in\mathbb R^p\) when sampling is invoked.
sampling_model.treatment: A latent regime selects either the observational SEM or exactly one perfect stochastic intervention target.
sampling_model.overlap: Every component weight is positive; quantitative lower weight and separation requirements belong to Open-ended Question 1.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Population theorems recover the finite Gaussian mixture up to permutation; finite-sample covariance recovery is not assumed and is isolated in Open-ended Question 1.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 10 states that the observational context is exactly the unique minimizer of the deviation-rank score.
Theorem 1 gives sufficiency and worst-case necessity of one intervention per latent node for recovery under the paper's causal-disentanglement setup.
Theorem 4.1 learns mixture parameters efficiently when the number of components is fixed.
Corollary 4.1.1 identifies the interventional Markov equivalence class using mixture samples plus separate observational samples under interventional faithfulness.

Theorem 3.1 uniquely identifies the intervention tuples and their weights from a pooled mixture of perfect interventions on a given finite discrete causal Bayesian network under positivity and exclusion.
Theorems 1 and 3 recover intervention targets and certain parents from designated observational and interventional samples using sparse precision differences under intervention faithfulness.
Theorem 1 proves consistency of UT-IGSP for the interventional Markov equivalence class and unknown targets under interventional faithfulness with segregated regimes.
Theorem 6 characterizes the interventional Markov equivalence class as the sparsest distribution-equivalent graphs under faithfulness, intervention heterogeneity, and model truthfulness.
Theorem 1.1 clusters growing centered nonspherical Gaussian mixtures under near-disjoint total-variation separation with dimension-polynomial cost and weight-dependent factors.
Theorems 4 and 6 give effective-rank operator-norm moment and concentration bounds for sample covariance operators from labeled Gaussian samples.

tldr: An unordered pooled mixture containing one observational centered Gaussian SEM component and one effective perfect stochastic intervention per labeled node determines its entire semantic explanation without faithfulness. Coordinate-isolated precision pairs identify baseline-root pairs, invariant root marginals orient the baseline, and acyclicity makes the row-support target matching unique. These facts yield a sound-and-complete \(O(p^4)\) exact membership certificate, legal low-dimensional counterfamilies to the ICML 2023 rank selector, an open-family impossibility for all equivariant rank-only selectors, and deterministic recovery under operator error below \(\min\{\lambda/2,\alpha\lambda^2/16,g/8\}\). The end-to-end growing-dimensional component-estimation tail remains an explicit open question.

project_justification.gap: The only published unknown-baseline reduction for this intervention geometry is Proposition 10 of Squires et al.; its decisive intervention-versus-intervention rank inequality is false, and its Appendix G concedes that rank at most two is only necessary for model membership. Kumar and Sinha identify pooled perfect-intervention components on a finite discrete causal Bayesian network only when the baseline network and observational law are given, under positivity and exclusion. Later Gaussian pooled-mixture work supplies observational data separately for causal discovery and invokes interventional faithfulness.
project_justification.niche: The observed-coordinate, centered, fully covered perfect-stochastic-intervention subclass has enough entrywise precision geometry to support universal identification at every legal parameter point, including unfaithful laws and nonroot interventions that preserve marginal noise variance.
project_justification.fill: The coordinate certificate recovers the baseline, target bijection, weighted DAG, structural and intervention variances, and mixture weights; it also certifies nonmembership, supplies a sharp information-loss diagnosis for rank-only selectors, and exposes the exact all-component margin needed for stable decoding.

related_work: Squires et al. (2023, Theorem 1 and Proposition 1) supply the causal-disentanglement setup and the precision-difference construction; their Appendix F.2 Proposition 10 is the theorem-level target replaced here, while Appendix G explicitly leaves complete membership testing open. Kumar and Sinha (2021, Definition 3.1, Assumptions 3.1 and 3.2, and Theorem 3.1) prove component and intervention-target identification for a pooled mixture of perfect interventions when the finite discrete baseline causal Bayesian network and its observational law are given, under positivity and exclusion. That theorem informs but does not subsume the present result because the observational component and baseline SEM are hidden here and must be recovered from centered Gaussian components. Kumar, Shiragur, and Uhler (2024, Theorem 4.1) motivate the pooled-mixture front end, but fix the number of components; their Corollary 4.1.1 additionally uses separate observational samples and interventional faithfulness, so it informs rather than subsumes the present semantic recovery theorem. Varici et al. (2021, Equation (6) and Theorems 1 and 3) provide the closest precision-support estimation machinery for a designated observational/interventional pair, but their diagonal screen and faithfulness-based guarantees do not select a hidden baseline. Squires, Wang, and Uhler (2020, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 1) establish UT-IGSP for segregated regimes under interventional faithfulness. Gamella et al. (2022, Theorem 6) characterize a Gaussian noise-intervention equivalence class under faithfulness and additional conditions, rather than a hidden-baseline collection of perfect surgeries. Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025, Definition 1.5) supply identifiability terminology; their Theorem 1.6 gives higher-order-cumulant perfect-intervention recovery under a known observational context and non-Gaussian errors, leaving the centered-Gaussian hidden-baseline problem untouched. Anderson et al. (2026, Theorem 1.1) and Koltchinskii and Lounici (2017, Theorems 4 and 6) provide the two techniques named in the open statistical handle: growing-component centered-mixture clustering and within-cluster operator-norm covariance concentration.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact certificate is a real-arithmetic population procedure. It does not test approximate equalities, certify rational bit complexity, recover individual latent regime labels for pooled observations, or provide an end-to-end component estimator. The causaldag documentation for unknown-target IGSP expects separate observational and interventional sufficient statistics and regime metadata. On an accepted exact tuple, the certificate can supply the semantic baseline and target labels that such a workflow needs, and it recovers the DAG directly within its narrower model. It cannot by itself manufacture segregated samples or the empirical conditional-independence and invariance testers required by that software interface; it is therefore a semantic validation and initialization layer, not a drop-in statistical replacement.
honest_scope: The population identification, membership, rank-obstruction, and deterministic stability claims are all to be proved. The statistical component-recovery rate is intentionally open. The reduction at \(p=2\) agrees with the known directed-chain regression formulas; when \(G\) is empty, every support is a singleton and the certificate reduces to recognizing a diagonal baseline with one coordinate variance changed in each other component. At \(p=1\), the two variances admit both baseline orientations, so the restriction \(p\ge2\) is necessary. Missing interventions, soft or multitarget interventions, latent coordinate mixing, cyclic systems, and singular components are outside the positive theorem.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the false lower bound on intervention-versus-intervention precision-difference rank by coordinate-isolated support geometry, then add global baseline factorization for sound membership.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the paper's Proposition 1 because every surgery has rank at most two. Rebuttal: rank loses the baseline-root symmetry and admits nonmember tuples; orientation, unique matching, and global factorization require new arguments.

seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The obstruction holds on a strict parameter region rather than at one hand-tuned law.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Interrogate the claimed strict rank-score gap by preserving the entire rank matrix under a baseline-root transposition on a strict parameter region.
seed_details.red_team: Only a numerical erratum. Rebuttal: the open one-root-star family rules out every permutation-equivariant rank-only selector, not merely the published score.

seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The rate and tail object are the statistical kernel; the estimation rung is not used as a bare motif.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed-component Gaussian-mixture learner by separation-preserving centered-mixture clustering, then propagate cluster contamination through effective-rank covariance concentration.
seed_details.destination_search: Anderson et al. (2026) cover growing centered nonspherical mixtures but only under near-disjoint total-variation separation and without the required surgery-specific operator-error tail.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by combining generic clustering with sample covariance concentration. Rebuttal: existing clustering guarantees do not provide the needed per-component operator error under the weak separations implied by effective surgeries, and contamination bias is load-bearing.

seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Uniform calibration and power, rather than a plug-in consistency claim, are the intended limit-theory objects.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace separate inverse-Wishart minor tests by simultaneous confidence regions propagated through the complete semantic certificate.
seed_details.red_team: A routine confidence-ball wrapper around continuity. Rebuttal: uniform power against nonmembers requires controlling discrete matching, equality strata, and label-switched dependent mixture estimates, which generic covariance balls do not settle.

literature_map.thread: Pooled perfect interventions on a known discrete baseline
literature_map.settled: Kumar and Sinha (2021, Theorem 3.1) uniquely identify intervention tuples and their weights from a pooled mixture of perfect interventions on a given finite discrete causal Bayesian network under Assumption 3.2 positivity and Assumption 3.1 exclusion.
literature_map.open_or_failed_boundary: Their theorem takes the baseline causal Bayesian network and its observational law as inputs; it therefore does not identify a hidden observational component, baseline DAG, or Gaussian structural parameters from an unordered centered-Gaussian collection.

literature_map.settled: Sparse precision differences can estimate targets and some parents for a designated observational/interventional pair.
literature_map.open_or_failed_boundary: The method assumes the baseline pairing and intervention faithfulness and uses diagonal changes that can vanish for legal nonroot perfect interventions here.

literature_map.settled: A distributional equivalence class is characterized for segregated Gaussian noise interventions under faithfulness and additional conditions.
literature_map.open_or_failed_boundary: It does not characterize the unordered hidden-baseline perfect-surgery tuple or its incomplete-coverage equivalence relation.

literature_map.settled: Strongly total-variation-separated centered mixtures admit dimension-polynomial clustering, and labeled Gaussian samples admit effective-rank covariance concentration.
literature_map.open_or_failed_boundary: Their combination does not yet yield the contamination-aware permutation-matched operator tail under primitive perfect-surgery margins.

literature_map.settled: Definition 1.5 supplies identifiability terminology, while Theorem 1.6 uses coupled higher-order cumulants to recover perfect-intervention latent structure under non-Gaussian errors and a known observational context.
literature_map.open_or_failed_boundary: Centered Gaussian components have no higher-order cumulant leverage, and the observational component remains hidden.

novelty_justification: The nearest theorem-level result is Squires et al. (2023), Appendix F.2 Proposition 10, whose strict rank-score claim fails on legal two-node models. The replacement uses coordinate support and invariant marginals absent from the rank matrix and includes an open-family impossibility theorem for every equivariant rank-only selector. Kumar and Sinha (2021, Theorem 3.1) uniquely identify intervention tuples and weights for pooled perfect interventions on a given finite discrete causal Bayesian network under positivity and exclusion, but their known observational context removes the hidden-baseline problem. Kumar et al. (2024) instead learn a fixed number of Gaussian mixture components and require separate observational samples plus interventional faithfulness for causal discovery. These results inform but do not provide universal hidden-baseline and target recovery, full parameter identification with unchanged nonroot variance, or a sound-and-complete arbitrary-tuple membership certificate.
message: Added the verified Kumar and Sinha UAI 2021 comparator throughout the bibliography, theorem-level novelty contrasts, structured comparator table, related work, literature map, and checklist. The core states that their Theorem 3.1 identifies pooled perfect-intervention tuples for a given finite discrete baseline causal Bayesian network under positivity and exclusion, whereas the observational component and baseline are hidden here. The corrected Leyes Carreno–Meroni–Seigal Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6 anchors are preserved.
